## Market notes
- Tape4Backup shows a site-wide banner: 'From September 1st, 2026, all LTO Tape prices have increased.' Despite that, its LTO-9 singles ($93.50-$99.50) and LTO-10 30TB singles ($256-$286.75) sit in line with other sellers. (https://www.tape4backup.com/collections/lto-9-tapes)
- Trend vs early 2026: LTO-9 cartridges flat (Symply quoted about $94 in Feb 2026; now $92-$112). LTO-10 30TB roughly flat to slightly down (Symply ~$280 in Feb 2026; now $256-$300). LTO-10 40TB lower than expected launch price (Symply expected ~$570 or $14.25/TB; now $491-$555 or $12.28-$13.88/TB). Symply blamed the 40TB premium on launch pricing, tight Aramid base film supply and hyperscaler deals. (https://gosymply.com/lto-10-40tb-update-is-the-extra-10tb-worth-the-cost/)
- DatacenterDisk (published 2026-08-17, data updated 2026-09-17): LTO tape 'largely stable at $4-$6/TB' while HDD prices rose sharply in 2026; tape's $/TB edge over HDD widened from about 2x to 3.5x. The stated reason is an independent supply chain (Fujifilm and Sony in Japan) that avoids the NAND shortage and hyperscale HDD demand. (https://datacenterdisk.com/news/hard-drive-prices-up-50-percent-2026)
- LTO Program (Sept 2026): 160.3 EB of LTO capacity shipped in 2025 (down 9% from the 176.5 EB record in 2024); Q1 2026 shipped capacity up 57% YoY, driven by LTO-9 adoption and the LTO-10 ramp; 2026 expected to set a new record. (https://www.lto.org/2026/09/lto-capacity-shipments-grow-57-yoy-in-q1-2026-as-ai-and-archive-demand-accelerates/)
- The Register (2026-09-02): only Sony and Fujifilm make LTO cartridges. Analyst Tom Coughlin tied the 2025 dip to 'the evolving international trade environment' making buyers more cautious (tariff-related caution, but no price figure given). (https://www.theregister.com/storage/2026/09/02/tape-still-isnt-dead-but-shipments-slipped-by-16-exabytes-in-2025/5293813)
- Blocks & Files (2026-09-04): suggests the 2025 dip may reflect buyers waiting for LTO-10; projects 2026 could reach about 251.67 EB if Q1 pace holds. (https://www.blocksandfiles.com/tape/2026/09/04/tape-capacity-shipments-fell-in-2025-but-2026-could-be-a-boom-year-for-tape/5294464)
- Fujifilm LTO Ultrium 10 40TB cartridge (16978170) uses an aramid base film and began shipping January 2026; it works in existing LTO-10 drives. IBM 40TB cartridges (models 564/664) available 2026-03-06. (https://www.storagenewsletter.com/2026/01/15/ibm-lto-10-40tb-data-cartridges-models-564-and-664/)
- Half-height LTO-10 drives: Symply support article said HH drives expected Q2 2026 (FH first because of the new head guide assembly). No HH LTO-10 drive was listed at any seller checked on 2026-09-17. (https://support.gosymply.com/support/solutions/articles/80001179382-about-lto-10)

## Buyer guides and analysis
- Tape Backup Software Integration Tradeoffs (https://tapebackup.org/blog/tape-backup-software-integration-tradeoffs, 2026-10-12): The tape systems that integrate best are the ones on your backup software's compatibility list. Current LTO drives and libraries from HPE, IBM, Quantum and Dell work with Veeam, Commvault and the other mainstream products when the exact model, firmware and host adapter are listed. The real tradeoffs sit in the software: built-in automation and a searchable catalogue against being able to read the tapes without that software.
- Tape Backup Energy Use and Operating Cost (https://tapebackup.org/blog/tape-backup-energy-use-and-operating-cost, 2026-10-12): A standalone LTO drive that is switched on only while it writes is the most energy-efficient way to keep an archive: a cartridge on a shelf uses no power at all. In our 500 TB model, a disk array kept online uses about 4,400 kWh a year, a small tape library left on all year about 800 kWh, and a standalone drive used only for writing about 16 kWh.
- Tape Encryption and Security, Side by Side (https://tapebackup.org/blog/tape-backup-encryption-security-compared, 2026-10-12): Every LTO drive from LTO-4 onward encrypts in hardware with AES-256, whichever brand is on the front, so the drive is not what separates one tape system from another. What differs is how the encryption keys are managed: by the backup software, by the tape library through an external key manager, or by the host's tape driver. Add WORM cartridges and a copy that is offline when ejected, and tape covers the threats disk and cloud copies struggle with.
- Tape Backup 5-Year TCO: Systems Compared (https://tapebackup.org/blog/tape-backup-5-year-total-cost-of-ownership, 2026-10-12): Over five years, an LTO-8 or LTO-9 system holding two copies is the cheapest way to keep 500 TB or more in the US: about $19,200 for LTO-8 and $26,900 for LTO-9 at September 2026 prices, against $27,660 for five years of Glacier Deep Archive before any restore. Below about 100 TB, cloud archive storage usually costs less unless you restore often.
- Best Value per TB in Tape Backup, US 2026 (https://tapebackup.org/blog/best-value-per-terabyte-tape-backup-us, 2026-10-12): On media alone, LTO-9 is the cheapest tape per terabyte in the US, at $5.14 to $6.20 per TB in September 2026. Once you count the drive, an LTO-8 system costs less per terabyte stored for almost any archive a single team runs, because an LTO-8 drive costs about $4,100 less than an LTO-9 drive. LTO-10 makes sense when density matters more than price.
- Tape Is Dead, Right? Then Why Are People Quietly Building Backup Systems Around It Again (https://tapebackup.org/blog/tape-is-dead-right-then-why-are-people-quietly-building-backup-systems-around-it-again, 2026-05-05): “Tape Is Dead, Right? Then Why Are People Quietly Building Backup Systems Around It Again”
- LTO Tape Backup Looks Brilliant Until the Workflow Starts Fighting Back (https://tapebackup.org/blog/lto-tape-backup-costs-workflow-reality, 2026-04-03): Cheap tapes make LTO look irresistible. This breaks down the real costs: drives, HBAs, libraries, catalogs, cleaning, restores, and daily operation.
